name: Indexability
description: Checks the page-level signals that decide whether search and AI engines may index it: the canonical link, meta robots / bot-specific meta noindex, nofollow or none directives, and a soft-404 heuristic. A page that is noindexed, canonicalized to another domain or looks like an error page will not be surfaced or cited by AI search.
inputs: page HTML <head>: meta[name="robots"] and any meta whose name contains 'bot' (case-insensitive)
rendered visible text of main content and of body (innerText)

scoring.summary: Three sub-checks run first. If any critical issue exists (a noindex/none directive, a soft 404, or a canonical on a different hostname) the check fails with 0. Otherwise score = 8 minus the canonical penalty (none 1, multiple 3, different URL on same host 2, self-referencing 0) minus 2 if any nofollow/none directive exists, floored at 0.

rules.condition: canonical: exactly one, and new URL(canonical.href).hostname !== new URL(currentUrl).hostname (www vs apex counts as different)
rules.message: Canonical points to different domain (critical issue)

rules.condition: canonical: exactly one, same hostname, normalizeUrl(canonical) === normalizeUrl(current). normalizeUrl = protocol//hostname+pathname+search, strip ONE trailing '/', lowercase; drops port and #fragment, keeps query string
canonical: exactly one, same hostname, normalized URLs differ (different path, query, or http vs https)

noindex: first meta[name="robots"] content (lowercased) contains substring 'none' OR 'noindex'; OR any meta[name*="bot" i] (e.g. robots, googlebot, bingbot, GPTBot) content contains 'none' or 'noindex'
nofollow: same metas, content contains 'nofollow' or 'none' (and no noindex, otherwise critical already)
soft404 signal A: document.title lowercased contains any of '404', 'not found', 'page not found', 'error', 'no encontrado', 'nicht gefunden'

soft404 signal B: word count of main content < 200. Main content = innerText of first match of 'main, article, [role="main"], .content, #content'; fallback body innerText with nav, footer, header, aside, script, style, noscript removed. Words = split on /\s+/
soft404 signal C: first 1000 chars of body innerText (lowercased) contain 'page not found' or '404'
soft404: 2 or more of signals A/B/C

scoring.status_mapping: Any critical issue: fail with 0. Otherwise score >= 6 pass, >= 4 warning, else fail. Reachable non-critical outcomes: 8, 7 (no canonical), 6 (other URL, or nofollow), 5 (multiple canonicals or no canonical + nofollow), 4, 3.

detect.source_procedure: Per page template/route: 1) Canonical: find <link rel="canonical"> in static *.html; Astro layouts (often href={Astro.url} or new URL(Astro.url.pathname, Astro.site)); Hugo baseof/head partials ({{ .Permalink }}) plus baseURL in hugo.toml; Eleventy _includes layouts with page.url and site url data; Next.js app router metadata.alternates.canonical (and metadataBase) in app/**/layout.tsx/page.tsx, pages router next/head; Vite SPA index.html. Count occurrences in the composed head (layout + page + SEO components; plugins like @astrojs/sitemap do not add canonicals but next-seo/astro-seo do). Compare the resolved host with the production host (from site/baseURL/metadataBase/vercel or netlify config/CNAME); treat www vs apex mismatch as critical. 2) Robots meta: grep for <meta name="robots"|googlebot|bingbot|...bot> and Next.js metadata.robots ({index:false} renders noindex, {follow:false} renders nofollow); flag substrings noindex, none, nofollow exactly as the extension does (including max-image-preview:none, which contains 'none'). Watch for env-conditional noindex (e.g. noindex on preview builds) and note it. 3) Soft 404: compute title keywords and approximate main-content word count from built HTML (main/article/[role=main]/.content/#content, else body minus nav/footer/header/aside/script/style/noscript), and check the first 1000 chars of visible body text for '404' or 'page not found'. Best done on build output; otherwise let a model estimate word count from template + content files.
detect.llm_criteria: Only for soft-404 when output HTML is unavailable: estimate whether the visible main content of the page has fewer than 200 words, whether the <title> contains 404/not found/error/no encontrado/nicht gefunden (substring, so 'Error handling guide' counts), and whether the first ~1000 characters of visible body text contain '404' or 'page not found' (this includes phone numbers or prices containing 404). Soft 404 = at least 2 of the 3.

parity.note: Canonical and meta robots are usually exact from templates or metadata exports, but host resolution depends on the production domain, and values injected by JS (SPA route changes, SEO plugins, tag managers) or CMS are invisible in source. Extension compares canonical against the actual visited URL (including http/https, query strings and trailing slash rules), which source can only approximate. Soft-404 depends on rendered innerText and word counts, which source can only estimate without a build. X-Robots-Tag headers are NOT part of this check (see httpBehavior).

fix_summary: Emit exactly one self-referencing absolute canonical per page on the production host (Astro layout <link rel="canonical" href={new URL(Astro.url.pathname, Astro.site)}>, Hugo {{ .Permalink }}, Eleventy site.url + page.url, Next.js metadataBase + alternates.canonical), and remove noindex/nofollow/none from production robots meta (Next.js metadata.robots). Soft-404 fixes (thin content, error words in titles) need user content and are assisted.
